inspections.note: Incidence graphs between k-faces and r-faces of regular polytopes are weakly norming.

inspections.anchor: Theorem 1.2. Reflection graphs are weakly norming.
inspections.note: Coset graphs of finite reflection groups are weakly norming.

problem.text: Which graphs define (weakly) norming functionals, with applications to Sidorenko's conjecture.

claims.text: Theorem 1.2: reflection graphs (coset graphs of finite reflection groups) are weakly norming; Theorem 1.1: (k, r)-incidence graphs of regular polytopes are weakly norming; Theorem 5.12: N-decomposable graphs for weakly norming N are Sidorenko; Conjectures 6.1 to 6.3 characterize norming through edge-transitivity under cut or stable involution groups.

assumptions.text: Finite reflection groups with simple reflections; the Euclidean embedding of a reflection graph; edge-transitivity under cut involutions.

methods.text: Iterated Cauchy-Schwarz along cut involutions encoded in Cauchy-Schwarz trees and percolating folding sequences; Coxeter-group length arguments; entropy for N-decompositions.

evidence.text: Complete proofs and worked examples (the 1-subdivision of K4, hypercubes, octahedron variants).

limitations.text: The positive classes are highly symmetric and biregular; the characterization of weakly norming graphs is conjectural; only the building-block use reaches less symmetric graphs.

relevance.text: Theorem 1.1 covers the vertex-face incidence graphs of the tetrahedron, octahedron and icosahedron, the only triangulated spheres whose incidence graphs are biregular; through the (0, 1)-incidence graphs it also shows that the 1-subdivisions of the graphs of regular polytopes (bipartite graphs of girth at least six) are weakly norming and hence Sidorenko, a foothold for the girth-six candidate.
